Research

From my MSc in Artificial Intelligence at De Montfort University, Dubai, awarded with Distinction.

MSc dissertation · 2025

Responsible AI for skin disease classification

Most skin-lesion models are judged on accuracy alone. I asked whether they are also fair, robust, trustworthy and explainable enough for a clinic. I trained EfficientNet-B0, ViT-S/16 and EfficientNetV2-S in PyTorch on HAM10000: 10,015 dermoscopic images across 7 classes.

Macro-AUROC, all three modelsabove 0.94
Macro-F1 before calibration0.54
Macro-F1 after calibration and threshold tuning0.67
FairnessPatients under 30 and rare body sites were served worst.
RobustnessThe Vision Transformer held up best to blur and compression.
TrustEfficientNetV2-S was most reliable when allowed to abstain.
ExplainabilityGrad-CAM showed most predictions focused on the lesion.
MSc module project

NLP chatbot

Sequence-to-sequence chatbots trained in PyTorch on the Cornell Movie-Dialogs corpus. I compared an LSTM encoder–decoder with attention against a CNN model, scoring both on BLEU, perplexity and token accuracy.

PyTorchLSTM + attentionCNN seq2seqBLEUNLTK
